core_obligations: Set-up (proof lines 8976-8984): a point of the localized site lying over the given point is represented by a functor, and the values of both functors are identified with pullbacks of representable sheaves.

The two commutative diagrams (proof lines 8985-9020): the author compares the morphism sets and the values of the functors in the localized and ambient sites, showing that the functor of the localized point is determined by the fibre over an element of the value of the given point at the object, and that conversely an element determines such a functor.
Conclusion (proof lines 9021-9027): the constructions are inverse to each other, which gives the asserted one to one correspondence.
proof_roadmap: Represent a point lying over the given point by a functor and identify the values of both functors with pullbacks of representables.
Compare the two commutative diagrams to extract an element of the value of the given point at the object, and conversely.
Check that the two constructions are inverse.
difficulty_reason: The lemma states that the construction attaching a point of the localized site to a point of the site together with an element of the value of that point at an object gives a bijection between such points lying over the given one and the elements themselves (statement lines 8966-8974). The proof is a complete argument: the values of the functors attached to the points are identified with pullbacks of representable sheaves (proof lines 8976-8984); the author compares the morphism sets and values in the two sites through two commutative diagrams, extracting an element from a point lying over the given point and conversely (proof lines 8985-9020); and the two constructions are checked to be inverse (proof lines 9021-9027). The non-formal content is the comparison of the two diagrams. The claim is H2: a structured argument with each input named.
